phase_0.boundary_condition: the sealed semiprime interior that contains factorization, Y re-entry, homolysis, and register annihilation
phase_0.domain_name: semiprime interior: split a semiprime into its two prime

AFWD.justification: directs the factor pair into Y re-entry and later advances the fused semiprime toward homolysis

AREV.justification: descends radical arms into the annihilation slot of the register

CLINK.justification: chains prime p and prime q into the ordered pair that receives Y re-entry

ENGAGR.justification: keeps the homolyzed radical pair and the register annihilation residue live at once

EVALF.justification: refutes a smaller divisor on prime q and refutes a drifting Y re-entry state

EVALT.justification: affirms prime p by witness and affirms the Y re-entry pair as stable

FFUSE.justification: rejoins the stabilized prime arms into the semiprime and later rejoins the homolytic arms through register annihilation

FSPLIT.justification: opens the semiprime into prime p and prime q, and later opens the fused whole into radical p and radical q

IFIX.justification: appends the annihilated residue to the register as an irreversible mark

IMSCRIB.justification: the semiprime names itself as a two-prime product and the factor pair names itself as the argument of Y

TANCH.justification: the closed product boundary that contains factorization, re-entry, homolysis, and annihilation

VINIT.justification: the number exists before factorization, with no prime arms named

phase_2.fuse_result: one stabilized semiprime state after Y re-entry
phase_2.rejoin_note: prime arms receive primality work, Y re-entry stabilizes the pair, the arms rejoin into the whole, and the later homolytic arms rejoin through register annihilation
phase_2.verdict_reason: Tri-ancestral reconnection over a transformed object — closes

phase_3.false_description: B4 F (10) — constructively refuted: a candidate divisor rejected on a prime arm
phase_3.true_description: B4 T (01) — constructively proven: a prime arm with a valid primality witness

steps.domain_action: semiprime interior is unopened and unassigned
the semiprime recognizes itself as a two-prime product
split the semiprime into prime factor p and prime factor q
prime factor p affirms its primality witness
prime factor q refutes any smaller divisor
bind prime factor p and prime factor q into an ordered factor pair
the factor pair recognizes itself as the argument of Y
drive the factor pair into Y fixed-point re-entry
open Y re-entry into self-application and fixed-point check
self-application affirms a stable factor pair
fixed-point check refutes a drifting factor pair
close Y re-entry into a stabilized factor pair
fuse the stabilized prime factors back into the whole semiprime
advance the fused semiprime toward homolytic radicalization
homolyze the fused semiprime into radical p and radical q
descend radical p and radical q into the register annihilation slot
annihilate radical p and radical q with the register into a single residue
hold the homolyzed radical memory and the register residue together
append the register residue as a permanent annihilation record
seal the semiprime interior at its closed boundary
